messages.content:
Two readers answered the same question about machines at work. Reader A used facts taken from a fact
store; each fact comes with the sentence it was taken from. Reader B read the documents directly and points at
sentences. Decide which answer the evidence supports. Use only the evidence shown; do not use what you know.

Rules:
- An answer is supported only if its evidence states it for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the
  same article and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline, the same condition the question
  states). Evidence about a neighbouring subject does not support an answer.
- When the two rest on texts of different rank, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's
  manual, then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.)
  wins over a ministerial decree (DM). A wording corrected by a corrigendum replaces the original wording.
- For a list, prefer the answer whose items are each stated by the evidence and that leaves none out.
- If reader B found nothing, decide only whether A's evidence really states A's answer for the exact subject.
- "same" means the two answers say the same thing. "neither" means neither answer is supported.
Return JSON only: {"reasoning": "two or three short sentences", "choice": "A" | "B" | "same" | "neither"}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: On 1 March 2027 a company that is neither the original manufacturer nor a non-professional user carries out a substantial modification of a machine placed on the market in February 2027. In what capacity (as which economic operator) does it answer for that machine under the act applicable on that day?

Answer A: "The company answers as a manufacturer: under Article 18 of the Regulation it is subject to the manufacturer's obligations and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility, provided the substantial modification affects the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly; the facts do not state the outcome otherwise."
Under Article 18 of the Regulation (applicable from 20 January 2027), the company carrying out the substantial modification on 1 March 2027 is subject to the obligations of the manufacturer and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility, where the modification affects the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly. The facts do not establish the position for other modifications.
Evidence of A:
- non-professional user modifying machinery for own use: becomesManufacturer = shall not be considered to be a manufacturer (condition: for his or her own use) | sentence: "A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall not be subject to the obligations on the manufacturer set out in Article 10." [REG, Art. 18]
- person who carries out substantial modification: hasObligation = ensure and declare on its sole responsibility | sentence: "The person who carries out the substantial modification shall in particular, but without prejudice to other obligations set out in Article 10, ensure and declare on its sole responsibility that the machinery or related product concerned is in conformity with the applicable requirements of this Regulation and shall apply the relevant conformity assessment procedure as provided in Article 25 (2), (3) and (4) of this Regulation." [REG, Art. 18]
- natural or legal person carrying out substantial modification: hasObligation = shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 (condition: if the substantial modification has an impact on the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery) | sentence: "Article 18 Other cases in which obligations of manufacturers apply A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 for that machinery or related product or, if the substantial modification has an impact on the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery, for that affected machinery or related product, as demonstrated in the risk assessment." [REG, Art. 18]
- non-professional user modifying machinery for own use: hasObligation = shall not be subject to the obligations on the manufacturer set out in Article 10 (condition: for his or her own use) | sentence: "A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall not be subject to the obligations on the manufacturer set out in Article 10." [REG, Art. 18]
- substantial modification: definedAs = a modification of machinery or a related product (condition: which is not foreseen or planned by the manufacturer) | sentence: "(16) ‘substantial modification’ means a modification of machinery or a related product, by physical or digital means after that machinery or related product has been placed on the market or put into service, which is not foreseen or planned by the manufacturer, and which affects the safety of that machinery or related product, by creating a new hazard, or by increasing an existing risk, which requires:" [REG, Art. 3(16)]
- products placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC: placingAllowedUntil = 20 January 2027 (condition: placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027) | sentence: "read: ‘ 20 January 2027 ’." [CORR, Corrigendum, point 6]
- Directive 2006/42/EC: repealedFrom = 20 January 2027 | sentence: "read: ‘ 20 January 2027 ’." [CORR, Corrigendum, point 5]
- Regulation: appliesFrom = 20 January 2027 (condition: However, the following Articles shall apply from the following dates) | sentence: "read: ‘ 20 January 2027 ’." [CORR, Corrigendum, point 10]

Answer B: "As the manufacturer: under Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 it is considered a manufacturer and bears the manufacturer's obligations for the modified machinery."
Under Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Machinery Regulation, applicable from 20 January 2027 per the corrigendum to Article 51/54), a person carrying out a substantial modification, other than a non-professional user for own use, is considered a manufacturer and subject to Article 10 manufacturer obligations.
Evidence of B:
- Found by search: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "Article 18 Other cases in which obligations of manufacturers apply A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 for that machinery or related product" [REG, Art. 18]
- Found by search: REG, Art. 18 | sentence: "A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall not be subject to the obligations on the manufacturer set out in Article 10." [REG, Art. 18]
- Found by search: REG, Art. 51(2) (corrected by the corrigendum (Corrigendum, point 5: '14 January 2027' now reads '20 January 2027')) | sentence: "Article 51 Repeals. 2. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 20 January 2027." [REG, Art. 51(2)]
- Found by search: CORR, Corrigendum, point 5 | sentence: "On page 38, Article 51, paragraph 2, first subparagraph: for: ‘ 14 January 2027 ’, read: ‘ 20 January 2027 ’." [CORR, Corrigendum, point 5]

response.text: {"reasoning": "Art. 18 says that any natural or legal person carrying out a substantial modification is considered a manufacturer, except a non-professional user modifying for own use. For the assembly case it narrows the scope to the affected machinery. Answer A wrongly makes the manufacturer status conditional on the modification affecting only machinery that is part of an assembly, and says the outcome is otherwise unstated. Answer B states the general rule correctly, and the Regulation applies on 1 March 2027 because the Directive is repealed from 20 January 2027.", "choice": "B"}
